result.contractTitle: Agreement and Plan of Merger - Five Prime Therapeutics
result.summary: This agreement outlines the terms for a corporate merger involving Five Prime Therapeutics, Inc. Key provisions include intellectual property definitions, termination conditions, and a termination fee of $76,000,000. Overall risk is moderate based on the assessed playbook criteria.

categoryScores.comment: R-V-LIAB-01 Not Addressed: The provided excerpts do not contain the standard vendor 12-month trailing fee liability cap or consequential damages waiver.
R-V-INDEM-01 Not Addressed: The excerpts lack a limited scope IP indemnity provision aligned with the playbook.
R-V-TERM-01 Partial: The agreement includes an End Date rather than a standard commercial SaaS commitment term and auto-renewal mechanism.
R-V-IP-01 Pass: The agreement comprehensively defines and protects intellectual property rights.
R-V-PAY-01 Not Addressed: Payment terms such as Net 30 and service suspension rights are absent from the provided text.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Advocates for maximum protections and strict closing conditions for the acquiring party.
agentPerspectives.stance: Aggressive on deal certainty and closing mechanics.
keyPoints: Enforces the $76,000,000 termination fee under specific breach conditions.
Relies on strict definitions of Company IP to protect acquired assets.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Ensure mutual closing conditions are clearly understood without undue penalty.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Focuses on closing the transaction efficiently while preserving commercial value.
agentPerspectives.stance: Pragmatic and focused on transactional milestones.
keyPoints: Clear timeline leading up to the December 4, 2021 End Date.
Allows ordinary course of business exceptions for operational flexibility.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Maintain operational flexibility during the pre-closing period.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Evaluates contract terms against the Vendor / Provider Commercial Shield playbook.
agentPerspectives.stance: Cautious regarding missing standard SaaS protections.
keyPoints: Liability cap and payment terms are absent from the excerpts.
IP protections are robustly defined but lack specific vendor shield clauses.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Insert standard liability caps, IP indemnities, and Net 30 payment terms.

redlines.originalText: Parent’s right to receive payment from the Company of the Termination Fee pursuant to Section 9.3(b) shall be the sole and exclusive remedy of the Parent Related Parties against the Company
redlines.proposedText: Parent’s right to receive payment from the Company of the Termination Fee pursuant to Section 9.3(b) shall be the sole and exclusive remedy of the Parent Related Parties against the Company, except in the case of intentional fraud or willful breach.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: The other side will argue that the Termination Fee serves as agreed liquidated damages and provides certainty and finality for both parties upon termination.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Uncapped exposure or absolute restriction on remedies leaves the company vulnerable if intentional misconduct occurs outside standard termination scenarios.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: A standard carve-out for intentional fraud or willful breach is customary to prevent bad faith actions from being shielded by a limitation of remedies.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can agree to the termination fee as sole remedy for ordinary breaches, but we must carve out intentional fraud or willful breach. Fallback: limit the exception strictly to knowing and intentional material breaches.

redlines.originalText: each Company Associate who is or was involved in the creation or development of any Intellectual Property Rights on behalf of the Company... has signed a written agreement containing a present assignment to the Company
redlines.proposedText: each Company Associate who is or was currently involved in the creation or development of any material Intellectual Property Rights on behalf of the Company... has signed a written agreement containing a present assignment to the Company

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: The other side will argue that clean IP ownership and mandatory present assignments from all developers are foundational for the valuation and protection of the acquired assets.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Absolute strict liability for every historical contractor creates severe breach risk if minor past gaps exist.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Qualifying the representation by materiality and focusing on current or core developers aligns with standard risk allocation.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We should limit this representation to material IP and reasonable knowledge standards regarding past contractors. Fallback: add a disclosure schedule exception for historical contractors.

redlines.originalText: the Company shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement pursuant to this Section 9.1(d)(ii) if the Company is then in material breach of any representation, warranty, covenant or obligation hereunder
redlines.proposedText: the Company shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement pursuant to this Section 9.1(d)(ii) if the Company is then in willful material breach of any representation, warranty, covenant or obligation hereunder

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: The other side will argue that a breaching party should not be permitted to terminate the contract while in default of its own obligations.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: A minor or inadvertent breach by the company could be weaponized to trap them in the contract and block a valid termination.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Restricting the forfeiture of termination rights to willful or uncured material breaches protects against bad-faith blocking tactics.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: A minor, curable operational breach should not forfeit our right to terminate for their major default. Fallback: allow termination if our breach is being actively cured.

redlines.originalText: In the event that Parent or its designee shall receive full payment pursuant to this Section 9.3(b), the receipt of the Termination Fee shall be deemed to be liquidated damages for any and all losses or damages suffered
redlines.proposedText: In the event that Parent or its designee shall receive full payment pursuant to this Section 9.3(b), the receipt of the Termination Fee shall be deemed to be liquidated damages for any and all losses or damages suffered, except in cases of willful breach.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: The other side will argue that the fee is a standard, negotiated deal protection measure compensating them for foregone opportunities during the transaction.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: A $76,000,000 fee acts as an extreme penalty if triggered by circumstances outside normal deal failure or if compounded by other claims.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Ensuring liquidated damages do not waive liability for egregious willful defaults maintains balance.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: The termination fee is substantial and should cover standard deal costs, but willful breaches require a remedy carve-out. Fallback: reaffirm the fee amount while adding the willful breach exception.

obligations.requirement: The Company shall promptly notify Parent of any Legal Proceeding commenced against the Company or its directors relating to the Transactions.
The Company shall pay, or shall cause to be paid, to Parent the Termination Fee by wire transfer of same day funds under specified termination conditions.
obligations.triggerOrDeadline: Upon termination of the agreement pursuant to Section 9.3(b)
obligations.breachConsequence: Liquidated damages for losses or damages suffered

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: Indemnified Persons is defined in Section 7.4(a) of this Agreement. Indemnifying Parties is defined in Section 7.4(b) of this Agreement.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Indemnification — Market Mutual IP & Third-Party Indemnification
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Provider Indemnification. Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer... (b) Customer Indemnification... (c) Procedure...
deviations: The provided excerpts only mention definitions for Indemnified Persons and Indemnifying Parties without spelling out mutual IP indemnification obligations.
missingProtections: Explicit third-party IP infringement indemnification and defense procedures are not detailed in the excerpt.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Review the full text of Section 7.4 to ensure comprehensive mutual indemnification protections are present.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the Laws of the State of Delaware... each of the Parties irrevocably and unconditionally consents and submits to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Governing Law — Clear Governing Law and Neutral Forum
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: This Agreement is governed by the laws of [agreed jurisdiction], without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction...
deviations: Specifies Delaware law and specific state/federal courts rather than generalized placeholders.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: The governing law and forum selection clauses are robust and clearly favor Delaware.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: Except as would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to be material to the Company, to the Knowledge of the Company, the consummation of the Transactions will not violate any Data Privacy and Security Requirement applicable to the Company.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Data Privacy & Security — SOC 2 Type II Security Covenants & 48-Hour Security Breach Notification
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Security Measures. Provider shall maintain administrative, physical, and technical safeguards... (b) Security Incident Notification... (c) Data Return & Destruction...
deviations: Contract addresses privacy and security compliance representations rather than ongoing affirmative operational security covenants or breach notification windows.
missingProtections: Specific 48-hour security breach notification and SOC 2 certification requirements are missing from the excerpts.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Incorporate explicit data security covenants and breach notification timelines if handling sensitive customer data.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: Amgen Inc. One Amgen Center Drive Thousand Oaks, California 91320-1799 Attention: Corporate Secretary... if to the Company: Five Prime Therapeutics, Inc. 111 Oyster Point Boulevard South San Francisco, CA 94080 Attention: Legal Department
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Notices — Written Notices with Defined Addresses
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: All notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by recognised courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses stated...
deviations: Excerpts list specific physical and email recipient addresses but omit general delivery method instructions.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Confirm that notice delivery methods and receipt effectiveness rules are fully detailed in the unquoted portions of Section 10.8.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: No Company Associate or other Person... owns or has any claim, right or interest to or in any Owned Company IP and each Company Associate who is or was involved in the creation or development of any Intellectual Property Rights... has signed a written agreement containing a present assignment
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: IP Ownership — Each Party Keeps Its Pre-Existing IP; Licence to Deliverables
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Each party retains all rights in its intellectual property existing before or developed independently of this Agreement. The Customer owns all deliverables created specifically for it upon payment...
deviations: Focuses on company employee assignment of IP rather than a commercial framework of pre-existing IP retention and deliverable licensing.
missingProtections: Explicit license grants for embedded provider materials in deliverables are absent.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Ensure standard commercial IP ownership and licensing clauses are added if deliverables are being custom-built.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: then, in any such event under this Section 9.3(b), the Company shall pay, or shall cause to be paid, to Parent the Termination Fee by wire transfer of same day funds... Termination Fee means a cash amount equal to $76,000,000.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Change of Control — Notice and Exit Right on Change of Control
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: A party undergoing a Change of Control shall notify the other party in writing within thirty (30) days. If the acquiring entity is a competitor...
deviations: Contract provisions address corporate acquisition termination fees and superior offers rather than a standard commercial change of control exit right.
missingProtections: Specific notice periods and competitor-based termination rights for commercial contracts are not present.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Add standard commercial change of control protections if this agreement governs ongoing vendor-client relationships.

rules.explanation: The provided excerpts do not contain the standard vendor 12-month trailing fee liability cap or consequential damages waiver.
rules.recommendation: Add a limitation of liability clause capping vendor total liability at the amounts actually received in the preceding 12 months.

rules.explanation: The excerpts lack a limited scope IP indemnity provision aligned with the playbook.
rules.recommendation: Include a standard IP indemnification clause covering infringement claims conditioned on prompt notice and sole defense control.

Payment terms such as Net 30 and service suspension rights are absent from the provided text.

missingProtections.title: Renewal with Reminder and Short Opt-Out Notice
missingProtections.standardText: This Agreement renews for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the current term. The Provider shall send a written renewal reminder, including any price change, at least sixty (60) days before each renewal date. Renewal fees may not increase by more than the lower of five percent (5%) or the applicable consumer price index.
missingProtections.evidence: This is a definitive merger or acquisition agreement rather than an ongoing commercial services contract, making renewal terms irrelevant.

opposingFindings.quote: Parent’s right to receive payment from the Company of the Termination Fee pursuant to Section 9.3(b) shall be the sole and exclusive remedy of the Parent Related Parties against the Company
opposingFindings.issue: The limitation of remedies restricts recovery exclusively to the Termination Fee, preventing broader damages for material breaches outside the termination triggers.
opposingFindings.leverage: The other side will argue that the Termination Fee serves as agreed liquidated damages and provides certainty and finality for both parties upon termination.

opposingFindings.quote: each Company Associate who is or was involved in the creation or development of any Intellectual Property Rights on behalf of the Company... has signed a written agreement containing a present assignment to the Company
opposingFindings.issue: Strict IP assignment representations create high exposure for past contractor or employee leakage if any chain of title is imperfect.
opposingFindings.leverage: The other side will argue that clean IP ownership and mandatory present assignments from all developers are foundational for the valuation and protection of the acquired assets.

opposingFindings.quote: the Company shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement pursuant to this Section 9.1(d)(ii) if the Company is then in material breach of any representation, warranty, covenant or obligation hereunder
opposingFindings.issue: Conditioning the Company's termination rights on an absolute lack of material breach creates an easily weaponized hurdle.
opposingFindings.leverage: The other side will argue that a breaching party should not be permitted to terminate the contract while in default of its own obligations.

opposingFindings.quote: In the event that Parent or its designee shall receive full payment pursuant to this Section 9.3(b), the receipt of the Termination Fee shall be deemed to be liquidated damages for any and all losses or damages suffered
opposingFindings.issue: The substantial Termination Fee of $76,000,000 acts as an onerous penalty on exit without reflecting actual proportional losses in certain scenarios.
opposingFindings.leverage: The other side will argue that the fee is a standard, negotiated deal protection measure compensating them for foregone opportunities during the transaction.
